tests.title: The rule builder grants every right beneath the writable roots, read and execute on the system and --landlock-ro roots, read only on /proc, read and write on the device files, and nothing else
given: directories W, H, T, R and O created under t.TempDir()
inputs: workdir W, explicit env HOME=H and TMPDIR=T, --landlock-rw R, --landlock-ro O, --network unrestricted
the confine package's rule-building step, called directly from its own tests without applying anything, for applied ABI 2, 3 and 4
tests.when: the rules and the report lists are built for each applied ABI
then: Writable contains exactly the resolved W, H, T and R plus those of /dev/null, /dev/zero, /dev/full, /dev/random and /dev/urandom that exist on the host
ReadOnly contains exactly the existing members of /usr, /bin, /sbin, /lib, /lib32, /lib64, /libx32, /etc and /opt, plus O and /proc
each writable-root rule carries every filesystem right the ABI defines: execute and refer at ABI 2, and truncate as well at ABI 3 and 4

each system and --landlock-ro rule carries exactly read-file, read-dir and execute; the /proc rule carries exactly read-file and read-dir; each device rule carries read-file and write-file and no execute or directory right; no rule names any other path

tests.title: In a re-executed child under the applied ruleset, the writable roots accept create, cross-directory rename, truncate and execute, and everything outside is denied with EACCES
given: Linux; the test's independent probe (syscall 444 with LANDLOCK_CREATE_RULESET_VERSION) reports kernel ABI 2 or later, else the test skips naming the ABI or error it found
directories W, H, T, R and O, a sibling directory S outside all of them holding S/secret, and O/ro.txt, all created by the parent
the test binary re-executed as a child with an environment marker selecting this case, so that the ruleset confines only the child
tests.when: the child applies the ruleset through confine's entry point with workdir W, HOME=H, TMPDIR=T, --landlock-rw R, --landlock-ro O and --network unrestricted, then performs the file operations below
then: creating a file under each of W, H, T and R succeeds; renaming W/a/f to W/b/f succeeds; at an applied ABI of 3 or more truncate(2) on W/b/f succeeds; a shell script written into W and executed exits 0
creating S/new, creating O/new and writing /proc/self/comm each fail with an error for which errors.Is(err, syscall.EACCES) is true; reading S/secret fails with EACCES
reading O/ro.txt and /etc/passwd, running /bin/sh -c true, reading /proc/self/status and running /bin/sh -c 'echo x > /dev/null' (an O_TRUNC open of a device file) all succeed
the child prints its completion marker and exits 0, and the parent asserts both so a silently skipped child fails
tests.pseudocode:
if probeKernel() < 2: t.Skipf('kernel Landlock ABI %d < 2', k)
child(case='fs'):
  info,err = confine.Setup(W, env, rw=[R], ro=[O], Unrestricted); assert err==nil && info.ABI>=2
  for d in [W,H,T,R]: assert create(d+'/x')==nil
  assert rename(W+'/a/f', W+'/b/f')==nil; if info.ABI>=3: assert truncate(W+'/b/f',0)==nil
  writeExec(W+'/s.sh'); assert run(W+'/s.sh')==0
  for p in [S+'/new', O+'/new']: assert errors.Is(create(p), EACCES)
  assert errors.Is(writeFile('/proc/self/comm','x'), EACCES); assert errors.Is(readFile(S+'/secret'), EACCES)
  assert readFile(O+'/ro.txt')==nil && run('/bin/sh','-c','true')==0 && readFile('/proc/self/status')==nil && run('/bin/sh','-c','echo x > /dev/null')==0
  print(marker); exit 0
parent: assert exit==0 && contains(out, marker)

tests.title: At applied ABI 4 the ruleset denies TCP bind and connect under none, loopback included, and leaves TCP alone under allowlist and unrestricted
given: Linux with kernel Landlock ABI 4 or later by the test's independent probe, else a skip naming the ABI found
a TCP listener the parent opened on 127.0.0.1:0, its address passed to the child
one re-executed child per network mode
tests.when: each child applies the ruleset with --network none, allowlist or unrestricted, then dials the parent's listener with a net.Dialer whose Multipath TCP is disabled and binds 127.0.0.1:0 through a net.ListenConfig whose Multipath TCP is disabled
then: under none, the report's TCP is true, the dial fails with EACCES and the bind fails with EACCES
under allowlist and under unrestricted, the report's TCP is false, the dial succeeds and the parent's listener accepts the connection, and the bind succeeds
each child exits 0 with its completion marker

tests.title: Missing system, device and flag paths are skipped, only the flag paths are noted, and the rest of the ruleset still applies
given: the system-directory and device-file lists, replaceable in the confine package's own tests, extended with /nonexistent-agentkit-sys and /dev/nonexistent-agentkit
absolute paths M1 and M2 under t.TempDir() that do not exist, passed as --landlock-ro M1 and --landlock-rw M2, with a valid workdir W
tests.when: the report is built, and on Linux with kernel ABI 2 or later a re-executed child applies the same inputs
then: none of the four missing paths appears in Writable or ReadOnly, and every existing root still does
Note contains M1 and M2 and contains neither /nonexistent-agentkit-sys nor /dev/nonexistent-agentkit
building returns no error, and the child's apply returns nil after which creating a file under W succeeds
tests.pseudocode:
withSystemDirs(append(sys,'/nonexistent-agentkit-sys')); withDevices(append(dev,'/dev/nonexistent-agentkit'))
r,err = buildRules(inputs{Workdir:W, RO:[M1], RW:[M2]}, 4); assert err==nil
for p in [M1,M2,'/nonexistent-agentkit-sys','/dev/nonexistent-agentkit']: assert p ∉ r.Writable ∪ r.ReadOnly
assert contains(r.Note,M1) && contains(r.Note,M2) && !contains(r.Note,'nonexistent-agentkit-sys') && !contains(r.Note,'/dev/nonexistent-agentkit')
if linux && probeKernel()>=2: child: _,err = confine.Setup(same); assert err==nil && create(W+'/x')==nil

tests.title: An unset, relative, missing, root or system-directory HOME or temporary directory is skipped with a note while the agent still starts and serves
given: a valid workdir W, a symlink L under t.TempDir() pointing to /usr, and a missing path X under t.TempDir()
the confine package's report-building step, and for the last case the built agentkit-sandboxd
tests.when: the report is built for HOME unset, HOME=rel/home, HOME=X, HOME=/, HOME=/etc and HOME=L, and for TMPDIR=rel/tmp, TMPDIR=X, TMPDIR=/, TMPDIR=/usr and TMPDIR unset with TEMP=X (13's fall-through order); then, on Linux with kernel ABI 2 or later, the binary is started with HOME=/ and TMPDIR=X
then: in every case the skipped root and its resolved path are absent from Writable, while W and the other, valid root remain
in every case Note names the variable that supplied the value (HOME, TMPDIR or TEMP) together with the offending value, or says it is unset, and building returns no error
the started binary answers Hello; its Agent().Landlock.ABI is above 0, Writable contains neither / nor X, and Note names both HOME and TMPDIR
tests.pseudocode:
for c in cases: r,err = buildRules(inputs{Workdir:W, Env:c.env}, 4); assert err==nil
  assert c.root ∉ r.Writable && resolved(c.root) ∉ r.Writable && W ∈ r.Writable
  assert contains(r.Note, c.var) && (c.unset ? contains(r.Note,'unset') : contains(r.Note, c.value))
if linux && probeKernel()>=2: p = start(bin,'--workdir',W, env=['HOME=/','TMPDIR='+X,'PATH=/usr/bin:/bin']); sb = attachTo(p)
  l = sb.Agent().Landlock; assert l.ABI>0 && '/' ∉ l.Writable && X ∉ l.Writable && contains(l.Note,'HOME') && contains(l.Note,'TMPDIR')

tests.title: A root or system-ancestor --workdir or --landlock-rw, or a relative --landlock-ro or --landlock-rw, exits 2 with one stderr line naming the flag
given: the agentkit-sandboxd binary built into t.TempDir(), run on Linux and macOS
a symlink L under t.TempDir() that points to /usr
tests.when: the binary is run, with stdin closed, with each of: --workdir /, --workdir /usr, --workdir L, --landlock-rw /, --landlock-rw /opt, --landlock-rw rel/dir, --landlock-ro rel/dir
then: each run exits with status 2
each run writes exactly one non-empty line to stderr containing the offending flag's name (--workdir, --landlock-rw or --landlock-ro)
each run writes nothing to stdout, so no Hello is ever served
tests.pseudocode:
for (args, flag) in [(['--workdir','/'],'--workdir'), (['--workdir','/usr'],'--workdir'), (['--workdir',L],'--workdir'), (['--landlock-rw','/'],'--landlock-rw'), (['--landlock-rw','/opt'],'--landlock-rw'), (['--landlock-rw','rel/dir'],'--landlock-rw'), (['--landlock-ro','rel/dir'],'--landlock-ro')]:
  so,se,code = run(bin, args...); assert code==2 && countLines(trim(se))==1 && contains(se, flag) && so==''

tests.title: For any set of roots, the report lists resolved, duplicate-free paths in the order their rules were added
given: a seeded generator of directory trees under t.TempDir() with real directories, symlinks to them, chains of symlinks, trailing slashes and .. components
the confine package's report-building step
tests.when: for any generated tree and any lists of --landlock-rw and --landlock-ro paths drawn from it (each root possibly repeated or named through different symlinks, with the resolved rw and ro sets kept disjoint), together with W, HOME and TMPDIR drawn from it, the report is built
then: Writable and ReadOnly each contain no duplicate
every entry e satisfies filepath.EvalSymlinks(e) == e

Writable equals the first-occurrence order of the resolved writable inputs in rule-addition order, followed or preceded only by the existing device files; ReadOnly likewise for read-only inputs, with /proc present in ReadOnly and absent from Writable
the number of rules equals the number of distinct resolved roots
tests.pseudocode:
for seed in 1..200: tree = genTree(seed); in = genInputs(tree, seed)
  r,err = buildRules(in, 4); assert err==nil
  assert noDup(r.Writable) && noDup(r.ReadOnly)
  for e in r.Writable ∪ r.ReadOnly: assert evalSymlinks(e)==e
  assert without(r.Writable, devices) == dedupFirst(map(resolve, rwOrder(in)))
  assert without(r.ReadOnly, systemDirs ∪ {'/proc'}) == dedupFirst(map(resolve, in.RO)) && '/proc' ∈ r.ReadOnly && '/proc' ∉ r.Writable
  assert len(r.rules) == len(distinct(resolved roots))

tests.title: Plan returns the ABI, TCP flag and note of the decision table for every kernel ABI from 0 to 8, a probe error and every network mode
given: confine.Plan, called from a test file with no build constraint so that it runs on every platform
tests.when: for every input in {kernel ABI 0..8} ∪ {probe error errors.New("boom")} crossed with {none, allowlist, unrestricted}, Plan(kernelABI, probeErr, mode) is called
then: probe error: ABI 0, TCP false, note `Landlock unavailable: boom`; kernel 0: ABI 0, TCP false, note `kernel reports no Landlock support`; kernel 1: ABI 0, TCP false, note `kernel Landlock ABI 1 cannot permit cross-directory renames (needs ABI 2, Linux 5.19); not applied` (all three in every mode)
kernel 2 or 3: ABI equals the kernel ABI and TCP is false; under none the note is exactly `kernel Landlock ABI k cannot restrict TCP (needs ABI 4, Linux 6.7)` with k the kernel ABI
kernel 4 to 8: ABI 4; TCP is true under none and false otherwise; the note is empty under none and under unrestricted

under allowlist at every input whose applied ABI is above 0 (kernel 2 to 8), TCP is false and the note states that Landlock cannot express a host allowlist and that TCP is left to the provider (it contains `allowlist` and `provider`)

tests.title: Plan lives in an unconstrained file and the kernel is probed exactly once per entry-point call through a replaceable seam
given: the confine package's source files parsed with go/parser and go/build/constraint
the unexported probe seam replaced by a counting fake in the package's tests
tests.when: the test finds the file declaring Plan and its test file, then calls confine's entry point with the fake returning 1, 2, 3 and a probe error
then: the file declaring Plan has no //go:build line and no GOOS or GOARCH file-name suffix, and neither does the test file exercising it
each call of the entry point invokes the fake exactly once, although both Plan and the report need its value

with the fake returning 1 or an error the outcome has ABI 0 and no ruleset is applied: the re-executed child performing those calls can still create a file outside every root afterwards; with 2 or 3 the outcome's ABI equals the simulated value (applied in a re-executed child on a kernel of at least that ABI, skipped otherwise)
tests.pseudocode:
f = fileDeclaring('Plan'); assert buildConstraint(f)==nil && !hasGOOSSuffix(f) && buildConstraint(testFileOf(f))==nil
child: n=0; withProbe(func(){n++; return v, e})
  for (v,e) in [(1,nil),(0,ENOSYS)]: n=0; info,_ = Setup(...); assert n==1 && info.ABI==0; assert create(outside)==nil
if probeKernel()>=3: child: for v in [2,3]: n=0; info,_=Setup(...); assert n==1 && info.ABI==v

tests.title: Applying sets no_new_privs, reaches every thread and every later process, and uses exactly the chosen version rather than the kernel's best
given: Linux with kernel Landlock ABI 2 or later by the test's independent probe, else a skip naming the ABI
re-executed children, a sibling directory S outside every root, a --landlock-ro root O holding O/f, and a loopback listener opened by the parent
tests.when: a child starts a goroutine pinned with runtime.LockOSThread that waits on a channel, applies the ruleset, then signals the goroutine; further children apply with the probe seam simulating ABI 2 on a kernel of ABI 3 or later and ABI 3 on a kernel of ABI 4 or later under none
then: prctl(PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS) returns 1 after the apply returns nil
the pinned goroutine, on its own OS thread, fails to create S/x with EACCES, and a grandchild `/bin/sh -c 'touch S/y'` exits non-zero with S/y absent
with ABI 2 simulated, truncate(2) on O/f succeeds (truncate is not handled by V2) while creating O/new fails; with ABI 3 simulated, truncate(2) on O/f fails with EACCES
with ABI 3 simulated under none, the dial to the parent's loopback listener succeeds and the report's TCP is false, showing RestrictPaths at V3 rather than Restrict at V4
tests.pseudocode:
child(threads): ch=make(chan struct{}); res=make(chan error); go func(){runtime.LockOSThread(); <-ch; res <- create(S+'/x')}()
  info,err = Setup(...); assert err==nil && prctl(PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS)==1
  close(ch); assert errors.Is(<-res, EACCES); assert run('/bin/sh','-c','touch '+S+'/y')!=0 && !exists(S+'/y')
if k>=3: child: withProbe(2); Setup(ro=[O]); assert truncate(O+'/f',0)==nil && errors.Is(create(O+'/new'),EACCES)
  child: withProbe(3); Setup(ro=[O]); assert errors.Is(truncate(O+'/f',0),EACCES)
if k>=4: child: withProbe(3); info,_=Setup(mode=none); assert !info.TCP && dial(ln.Addr())==nil

tests.title: A probe failure is not fatal: the outcome is ABI 0 with the unavailable note, nothing is applied, and an agent given that outcome serves and reports it
given: the probe seam replaced by a fake returning syscall.ENOSYS, syscall.EOPNOTSUPP and syscall.EPERM in turn, inside a re-executed child
an agent.Agent served over net.Pipe and reached through attach.Dial
tests.when: the child calls confine's entry point for each error, and the parent builds an agent with Config.Landlock set to the outcome the child printed
then: each call returns a nil error and LandlockInfo{ABI: 0, KernelABI: 0, TCP: false, Note: "Landlock unavailable: " + err.Error()} with empty Writable and ReadOnly
after the calls the child can still create a file outside every root and connect to a loopback listener, so nothing was applied
the agent built with that outcome answers Hello and Agent().Landlock equals it
tests.pseudocode:
child: for e in [ENOSYS, EOPNOTSUPP, EPERM]: withProbe(0, e); info,err = Setup(...)
  assert err==nil && info.ABI==0 && info.KernelABI==0 && !info.TCP && info.Note=='Landlock unavailable: '+e.Error() && len(info.Writable)==0 && len(info.ReadOnly)==0
  assert create(outside)==nil && dial(loopback)==nil; printJSON(info)
parent: a = agent.New(agent.Config{Workdir:t.TempDir(), TTL:time.Hour, Landlock:info}); sb = attachOverPipe(a); assert reflect.DeepEqual(sb.Agent().Landlock, info)

tests.title: A ruleset that cannot be built after a successful probe ends the command with one landlock line on stderr and exit status 1, serving nothing
given: Linux with kernel Landlock ABI 2 or later, the test not running as root (else a skip naming the reason)
the built agentkit-sandboxd and a directory P with mode 000 so that the absolute path P/sub cannot be resolved (EACCES, not ENOENT)
in the confine package, on a kernel offering exactly ABI 2 or 3, a re-executed child with the probe seam reporting 4
tests.when: the binary is started over pipes with --workdir W --landlock-ro P/sub and the test tries to attach; on an ABI 2 or 3 kernel the child calls confine's entry point
then: the process exits with status 1
stderr holds exactly one line, beginning `agentkit-sandboxd: landlock: ` and naming P/sub or the cause
nothing is written to stdout and the attach attempt fails without a Hello response
on an ABI 2 or 3 kernel, the entry point with the probe reporting 4 returns a non-nil error (V4 unsupported) instead of a weaker ruleset
tests.pseudocode:
if os.Getuid()==0: t.Skip('root bypasses the mode-000 directory'); mkdir(P,0o000)
p = start(bin,'--workdir',W,'--landlock-ro',P+'/sub'); _,err = attachTo(p); assert err!=nil
assert p.Wait().ExitCode()==1; se=stderr(p); assert countLines(trim(se))==1 && strings.HasPrefix(se,'agentkit-sandboxd: landlock: ') && stdout(p)==''
if k in [2,3]: child: withProbe(4); _,err = Setup(...); assert err!=nil

then: the stub file's constraint is satisfied for darwin and windows and not for linux, and it imports no package under github.com/landlock-lsm/go-landlock

tests.title: The report's KernelABI is the probe's value, unchanged by the cap at 4, and 0 after a probe error
given: the confine package's step that combines the probe result with Plan into a LandlockInfo before applying, with the probe seam replaced by a fake
tests.when: the outcome is computed for probe values 6 under none, 8 under unrestricted, 3 under none, 1 under none and a probe error under none
then: 6 under none gives ABI 4, KernelABI 6 and TCP true
8 under unrestricted gives ABI 4, KernelABI 8 and TCP false
3 gives ABI 3 and KernelABI 3; 1 gives ABI 0 and KernelABI 1; a probe error gives ABI 0 and KernelABI 0
tests.pseudocode:
for (v,e,mode,want) in [(6,nil,none,{4,6,true}), (8,nil,unrestricted,{4,8,false}), (3,nil,none,{3,3,false}), (1,nil,none,{0,1,false}), (0,ENOSYS,none,{0,0,false})]:

tests.title: parseFlags accepts --network with default none and repeatable --landlock-ro and --landlock-rw in order, and defines no flag that disables confinement
given: the command's parseFlags exercised in-package
tests.when: parseFlags runs on no arguments, on --network allowlist, on --network unrestricted, and on --landlock-ro /a --landlock-rw /x --landlock-ro /b --landlock-rw /y, and the test lists every flag the command's flag set defines
then: with no --network the parsed mode is none; allowlist and unrestricted parse to their modes
the parsed --landlock-ro values are [/a, /b] and the --landlock-rw values are [/x, /y], in command-line order
the flag set defines exactly workdir, ttl, version, network, landlock-ro and landlock-rw

cfg,_ = parseFlags([]); assert cfg.Network==sandbox.NetworkNone

assert flagNames(newFlagSet()) == {'workdir','ttl','version','network','landlock-ro','landlock-rw'}

tests.title: An AST test pins main's order: flags, then --version, then confinement, then redirectStdout, agent.New, goroutines and serving
given: the non-test Go files of sandbox/cmd/agentkit-sandboxd parsed with go/parser
synthetic sources in which agent.New, redirectStdout or a go statement precedes the confinement call, or the confinement call precedes the --version return
tests.when: the checker walks main and the package-local functions main calls directly, recording the source positions of the parseFlags call, the --version branch's return or exit, the call into sandbox/internal/confine, redirectStdout, agent.New and every go statement
then: on the real source, parseFlags precedes the --version branch, the --version branch returns before the confinement call, and the confinement call precedes every redirectStdout call, every agent.New call and every go statement
on each synthetic source the checker fails with a message naming the file and line of the offending call or statement
the real source contains exactly one confinement call, so the test is not vacuous

pos = positions(parse(cmdDir), roots=['main'])
assert pos.parseFlags < pos.versionReturn < pos.confine

assert len(pos.confineCalls)==1
for src in badSources: err = checkOrder(src); assert err!=nil && matches(err, file+':'+line)

tests.title: The command hands its confinement outcome to the agent, Hello reflects it, and processes started by tools inherit the ruleset
given: the agentkit-sandboxd binary built into t.TempDir(), started over pipes with --workdir W and HOME, TMPDIR and PATH=/usr/bin:/bin in cmd.Env
the test's independent probe of the kernel ABI k, and a sibling directory S outside every root
tests.when: the test attaches with attach.Dial over stdioconn, reads Agent().Landlock, and on an applied ABI above 0 runs a proxy execute of /bin/sh -c '/bin/sh -c "echo x > S/f"'
then: on Linux with k >= 2: ABI == min(k, 4), KernelABI == k and Writable contains the resolved W; with k < 2 or a probe error: ABI 0 and Plan's note; on macOS: ABI 0 and `Landlock is Linux-only (GOOS=darwin)`

tests.title: For any effective spec, AgentArgs produces flags that the command's parseFlags reads back as the spec's TTL, network mode and workdir
given: a test in the command's package with access to parseFlags and sandbox.AgentArgs

tests.when: for any generated effective spec, args = sandbox.AgentArgs(spec) is parsed with parseFlags
then: parseFlags returns no error, cfg.TTL == spec.TTL and cfg.Network == spec.Network.Mode
cfg.Workdir == spec.Workdir when Workdir is set, else the command's default /workspace
args contains --ttl followed by spec.TTL.String() and --network followed by spec.Network.Mode.String(), and contains --workdir exactly when spec.Workdir is non-empty

tests.title: HelloResponse carries LandlockReport landlock = 7 with the six specified fields, and the regenerated code passes the staleness check offline
given: the checked-in sandbox/internal/sandboxpb generated code and its hash file
tests.when: the test inspects sandboxpb.File_sandbox_proto through protoreflect and runs 13's staleness check with PATH emptied
then: HelloResponse has field 7 named landlock of message type LandlockReport, and its fields 1 to 6 are unchanged
LandlockReport has exactly abi = 1 (uint32), kernel_abi = 2 (uint32), tcp = 3 (bool), note = 4 (string), writable = 5 (repeated string) and read_only = 6 (repeated string)
the staleness check passes for the checked-in sandbox.proto and hash file without running protoc
tests.pseudocode:

tests.title: An embedder requiring Landlock starts the confined agent with AgentArgs, syncs a project over Rsync, runs a shell tool and exports the result
given: Linux with kernel Landlock ABI 4 or later, else a skip naming the ABI found
the built agentkit-sandboxd, a workspace directory W, HOME=H, TMPDIR=T, a host project directory P and an empty host directory D
Capabilities{Provider: "test", Network: [NetworkNone], Workdir: true, Landlock: true}
tests.when: the test computes eff = CheckSpec(caps, Spec{RequireLandlock: true, Network: {Mode: NetworkNone}, Workdir: W}), starts the binary with sandbox.AgentArgs(eff) over pipes, calls attach.New with Provider "test", Spec eff and a destroy step that waits for the process, then calls Sync(LocalDir{Path: P}), a proxy execute of /bin/sh -c 'mkdir -p out && echo hello > out/result.txt', and Export("out", LocalDir{Path: D})
then: attach.New returns a live Sandbox with Agent().ProtocolMinor 2 and Agent().Landlock ABI 4 and TCP true
Sync returns nil and P's files exist under W; the execute exits 0
Export returns nil and D holds result.txt containing `hello\n`
Close runs the destroy step once and the agent exits 0
tests.pseudocode:
if probeKernel()<4: t.Skipf(...)
eff,err = CheckSpec(caps, Spec{RequireLandlock:true, Network:{Mode:None}, Workdir:W}); assert err==nil
p = start(bin, sandbox.AgentArgs(eff)..., env=['HOME='+H,'TMPDIR='+T,'PATH=/usr/bin:/bin'])
sb,err = attach.New(ctx, attach.Config{Provider:'test', Spec:eff, Destroy:waitFor(p), conn:stdioconn.New(p.stdout,p.stdin)}); assert err==nil && sb.Agent().ProtocolMinor==2 && sb.Agent().Landlock.ABI==4 && sb.Agent().Landlock.TCP
assert sb.Sync(ctx,LocalDir{Path:P})==nil && filesUnder(W) ⊇ files(P)
assert execute(sb,`/bin/sh -c 'mkdir -p out && echo hello > out/result.txt'`).exit==0
assert sb.Export(ctx,'out',LocalDir{Path:D})==nil && read(D+'/result.txt')=='hello\n'
sb.Close(); assert destroys==1 && p.ExitCode()==0
